**Visual analysis of test image:**
- Macro/close-up view of fibrous stalk tissue (orange-tan background with longitudinal striations)
- Clearly visible **black spiny fruiting structures with setae** (bristle-like projections) — classic Colletotrichum acervuli
- Dark black blotches/lesions coalescing on the stalk rind tissue

**Reasoning:**
The black spiny setae on the fruiting bodies are the hallmark of Colletotrichum (anthracnose). The tissue is clearly stalk (fibrous, striated), not leaf. The dark blotches on the rind match the "shiny black discoloration" and "large black blotches" described for Anthracnose_stalk_rot. The reference collage confirms this: bottom-left panel shows identical shiny black stalk rind lesions, and upper-right shows the shredded/darkened pith interior.
